plan: With 3 bidders and values uniform on [0,49], the Nash equilibrium bidding strategy in a first-price auction is to bid (n-1)/n times your value, i.e., shade by 1/3. This balances the trade-off between probability of winning and profit margin. My value is $26, so optimal bid ≈ 26 × (2/3) = $17.3. This maximizes expected profit given rational competitors following similar strategies.

With 3 bidders and uniform values on [0,49], the standard Bayesian-Nash equilibrium bid for a first-price auction is value × (n-1)/n = value × 2/3. This balances winning probability against profit margin, avoiding overpaying while still competitively bidding. Given my value of $18, I'll bid $12, which follows this equilibrium strategy and should maximize expected profit against similarly rational opponents.

With uniform values on $0-49 and 3 bidders in a first-price auction, the optimal bidding strategy is to shade my bid to (n-1)/n of my value, which is 2/3 for n=3. My value is $21, so I should bid approximately $14 to maximize expected profit while maintaining a good chance of winning.
